intended_object: Given an R-derivation d : A → M, the induced R-derivation A[X] → M[X] that applies d to each coefficient, Σ aᵢXⁱ ↦ Σ d(aᵢ)Xⁱ. Here M[X] is PolynomialModule A M, an A[X]-module. Inferred from the docstring and the name.
explanation: The underlying linear map identifies A[X] with PolynomialModule A A and then maps each coefficient by d (PolynomialModule.map A d.toLinearMap). That is exactly coefficientwise application of d. It sends 1 to 0 because d(1) = 0. The Leibniz rule holds: the coefficient of X^k in d(pq) is Σ_{i+j=k} (aᵢ d(bⱼ) + bⱼ d(aᵢ)), which is the coefficient of X^k in p • d(q) + q • d(p). The proof checks this on monomials and extends it by additivity. The setting is general: any commutative base ring R, any R-algebra A and any module M over both. The use of commutative rings rather than semirings is presumably required by PolynomialModule (its instances were not checked). No more general Mathlib construction exists, since this declaration is Mathlib's own definition.
